metadata.title: ShadeRoute Scientific Bibliography & Institutional Documentation
metadata.study_area: Bhubaneswar, Odisha (SOA ITER Campus & Surrounding 3 km² Neighborhood)
metadata.plain_english_summary: All satellite indices (NDVI, LST, NDWI, BSI, NDBI) come from standard 900 m² satellite imagery (Landsat & Sentinel-5P) processed automatically via Google Earth Engine and ground-verified through on-site campus visits. All weather data (solar radiation, air temperature, humidity %, and atmospheric pressure) come from NASA POWER (MERRA-2) from 2.1.2015 to 12.5.2026. Formulas for pedestrian walking exposure and vulnerability were formulated in-house by Team Pipeline Pilots based on direct scientific and biometeorological principles.

citations.title: Landsat Satellite Earth Observation & Surface Temperature
citations.authors: U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) & NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
citations.venue: USGS EROS Data Center / Google Earth Engine Collections
citations.implementation_role: Standard satellite imagery with a 900 m² (30m × 30m) pixel resolution. Used through automated Google Earth Engine workflows to extract Land Surface Temperature (LST), vegetation cover (NDVI), moisture (NDWI), bare ground (BSI), and built concrete (NDBI). Primarily utilized for campus cooling simulation and tree/misting intervention planning.
citations.formula_mapping: Pixel Resolution: 30m × 30m (900 m² ground footprint per satellite pixel)
citations.apa_citation: U.S. Geological Survey & NASA. (2022). Landsat thermal infrared sensor calibration and surface temperature data. USGS EROS Data Center.

citations.title: Sentinel-5 Precursor Satellite Atmospheric & Optical Imagery
citations.venue: ESA Copernicus Open Access Hub / Google Earth Engine
citations.implementation_role: Standard satellite imagery (~900 m² gridded resolution) providing optical and atmospheric layers used alongside Landsat for campus environmental characterization and cooling simulation.
citations.formula_mapping: Satellite Resolution: ~900 m² gridded observation product
citations.apa_citation: European Space Agency. (2021). Sentinel-5 Precursor atmospheric products guide. ESA Copernicus Programme.

citations.title: NASA POWER / MERRA-2 Satellite Meteorological Reanalysis
citations.authors: NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO) & Langley Research Center
citations.venue: NASA Applied Sciences Program Meteorological Database
citations.implementation_role: Supplies all core meteorological weather inputs: solar radiation, air temperature (°C), relative humidity (%), atmospheric pressure, and wind speed. These weather records, combined with LST and NDVI across the entire 3 km² neighborhood polygon, are used to map heat stress (HI_IMD & HHSI) and train the heatwave forecast model.
citations.formula_mapping: Weather Inputs: Solar Rad (W/m²) + Air Temp (°C) + Humidity (%) + Atm Pressure (from 2.1.2015 to 12.5.2026)
citations.apa_citation: NASA GMAO. (2024). MERRA-2 meteorological and solar radiation dataset via NASA POWER. NASA Langley Research Center.

citations.title: OpenStreetMap Base Map & Team Pipeline Pilots On-Site Campus Survey
citations.venue: Open Data Commons (ODbL) & Field Ground Survey (SOA ITER Campus)
citations.implementation_role: OpenStreetMap serves as the street basemap foundation. The SOA ITER campus buildings layer, vegetation cover outlines, and pedestrian walkways/roads were manually drawn, sketched, and digitized by Team Pipeline Pilots based on high-resolution satellite imagery and physical on-site verification visits.
citations.formula_mapping: Base Map: OpenStreetMap | Campus Layers: Team On-Site Digitization & Field Verification
citations.apa_citation: Team Pipeline Pilots & OpenStreetMap Contributors. (2026). SOA ITER campus spatial digitization and OpenStreetMap cartographic base. ShadeRoute Project.

citations.title: The Heat Index Equation (Apparent 'Feels-Like' Temperature)
citations.venue: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Weather Service SR 90-23
citations.implementation_role: Mathematical equation used worldwide to calculate how hot the air actually feels to the human body by combining dry-bulb air temperature (°C) and relative humidity (%).
citations.apa_citation: Rothfusz, L. P. (1990). The heat index equation. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, NWS Technical Attachment SR 90-23.

citations.title: IMD 5-Tier Heat Hazard Classification & Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
citations.authors: India Meteorological Department (IMD), Ministry of Earth Sciences, Govt. of India
citations.venue: Ministry of Earth Sciences, New Delhi
citations.implementation_role: HI_IMD is calculated to divide the neighborhood into 5 danger categories based on official IMD criteria: Safe/Normal (<32°C), Caution (32–40°C), Extreme Caution (41–46°C), Danger (47–53°C), and Extreme Danger (>54°C). For the Human Heat Stress Index (HHSI), our team incorporated extra demographic vulnerability parameters to assess elevated heat risk for infants below 6 years and elderly citizens above 60 years.
citations.formula_mapping: IMD 5 Tiers: Normal (<32°C) | Caution (32–40°C) | Extreme Caution (41–46°C) | Danger (47–53°C) | Extreme Danger (>54°C)
citations.apa_citation: India Meteorological Department. (2023). Standard operating procedure for heat wave forecasting, warning and dissemination. Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India.

citations.title: ShadeRoute 3-Day Heatwave Prediction Model (Trained on 2015–2026 Data)
citations.implementation_role: Random Forest forecast model predicting heatwave risk across +1, +2, and +3 day horizons. Trained and tested on 11+ years of historical hourly spatial and weather data spanning from 2 January 2015 to 12 May 2026 (2.1.2015 to 12.5.2026), using strictly pre-forecast data to predict 13, 14, and 15 May 2026.
citations.formula_mapping: Training Dataset: Hourly Weather & Spatial Data (2.1.2015 to 12.5.2026) | Model: Horizon-Specific Random Forest Classifiers
citations.apa_citation: Team Pipeline Pilots. (2026). Machine learning heatwave prediction engine trained on 2015–2026 historical meteorological data. ShadeRoute Technical Report.

citations.title: ECMWF Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) NWP via Open-Meteo Live API
citations.authors: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) & Open-Meteo
citations.venue: ECMWF Open Data Portal & Open-Meteo Weather API
citations.implementation_role: Supplies live and historical numerical weather prediction (NWP) variables for Bhubaneswar (20.25°N, 85.80°E): surface pressure, precipitation probability, convective showers, CAPE, cloud cover, and wind. Directly feeds the V2 post-processing model and enables detection of rapid barometric pressure drops and convective storm suppression.
citations.formula_mapping: Live NWP Inputs: T2m + RH + PS + Rain + CAPE + Wind Gusts across +1 to +3 day horizons
citations.apa_citation: ECMWF & Open-Meteo. (2024). High-resolution numerical weather prediction data and global atmospheric forecasts. ECMWF Open Data.

citations.title: Early Detection of Extreme Weather Events via the ECMWF Extreme Forecast Index (EFI)
citations.venue: Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society, 132(617), 1257–1278
citations.implementation_role: Provides the peer-reviewed biometeorological basis for detecting anomalous heatwave conditions against ensemble climatology while factoring in convective instability and barometric pressure drops.
citations.formula_mapping: EFI = (2/pi) integral [ (F(x) - F_clim(x)) / sqrt(F_clim(x) * (1 - F_clim(x))) ] dx
citations.apa_citation: Zsótér, E. (2006). Recent developments in extreme weather forecasting: The Extreme Forecast Index. Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society, 132(617), 1257–1278.

citations.title: Google Earth Engine Automated Spectral Indices & On-Site Tree Ground-Truthing
citations.authors: Google Earth Engine (GEE) Platform & Team Pipeline Pilots Field Inspection
citations.venue: Google Earth Engine Automated Pipeline / On-Site Campus Field Survey
citations.implementation_role: All spectral indices—NDVI (Tree/Plant Canopy), NDWI (Moisture), BSI (Bare Soil), and NDBI (Concrete/Built-up)—were derived directly through automated Google Earth Engine cloud pipelines from Landsat (900 m²) and Sentinel-5P imagery, rather than manual formula calculation. To ground-truth these satellite numbers, our team conducted physical on-site visits across the SOA campus to inspect tree canopy cover, shadow corridors, and open concrete pathways.
citations.formula_mapping: Indices: NDVI = (NIR-Red)/(NIR+Red) | NDBI = (SWIR1-NIR)/(SWIR1+NIR) | BSI = Bare Soil | NDWI = Moisture (Computed automatically in GEE)
citations.apa_citation: Team Pipeline Pilots & Google Earth Engine. (2026). Automated satellite spectral indices and on-site tree canopy ground-truthing survey. ShadeRoute Remote Sensing Documentation.

citations.title: ExtraTreesRegressor Campus Vegetation Fraction & Priority Intervention Engine
citations.implementation_role: Our final ensemble machine learning regression model (ExtraTreesRegressor, 500 estimators, random_state=2026) trained on 5 spectral and thermal features (NDVI, NDBI, BSI, NDWI, LST). It calculates the continuous vegetation fraction (displayed as Veg% / Tree Cover % in the interface) across all 1,323 sample points of the SOA ITER campus. That predicted vegetation fraction is then directly utilized by the Priority Engine (priority_engine.py) to compute vegetation deficit (weighted at 35%) and recommend targeted cooling interventions: tree planting on open bare zones and misting sprayers along active pedestrian paths.
citations.formula_mapping: ML Model: ExtraTreesRegressor(NDVI, NDBI, BSI, NDWI, LST) -> Veg% / Vegetation Fraction -> Priority Engine (35% VegDeficit)
citations.apa_citation: Team Pipeline Pilots. (2026). ExtraTreesRegressor vegetation fraction prediction and priority cooling intervention engine. ShadeRoute Technical Documentation.

citations.title: Pedestrian Heat Exposure Index (In-House Scientific Formulation)
citations.implementation_role: Developed in-house by our team because no published journal paper provided an off-the-shelf micro-routing formula for campus footpaths. Grounded in biometeorological first principles: outdoor walking heat strain is a product of ground baking heat (normalized Landsat LST) magnified by the absence of overhead tree shade (1 - NDVI). Where ground surface temperature is hottest and shade is absent, pedestrian danger is maximal.
citations.formula_mapping: Pedestrian Exposure = LST_norm × (1 - NDVI_norm) [In-House First-Principles Formula]
citations.apa_citation: Team Pipeline Pilots. (2026). Pedestrian heat exposure index derived from surface temperature and shade deficit. ShadeRoute Analytical Framework.

citations.title: Composite Vulnerability Index (VI) (In-House Scientific Formulation)
citations.implementation_role: Formulated in-house by Team Pipeline Pilots to quantify neighborhood vulnerability across the 3 km² study zone. It combines three logical, evidence-based pillars: (1) Density of populations most vulnerable to heatstroke (infants under 6 years and senior citizens over 60 years), (2) Proximity to emergency hospitals and schools, and (3) Lack of cooling tree canopy.
citations.apa_citation: Team Pipeline Pilots. (2026). Multi-criteria demographic and spatial heat vulnerability index. ShadeRoute Analytical Framework.

citations.title: Heat–Health Action Plans: Guidance (2nd Edition)
citations.authors: World Health Organization (WHO Regional Office for Europe / Global Heat Health)
citations.venue: WHO Guidelines Approved by the Guidelines Review Committee, Geneva
citations.implementation_role: Guides tiered hospital emergency preparedness thresholds, oral rehydration stations, and casualty influx ratios used in hospital planning during heatwaves.
citations.formula_mapping: Surge Response Tiers: Yellow (Level 1), Orange (Level 2), Red (Level 3 Emergency)
citations.apa_citation: World Health Organization. (2024). Heat–health action plans: Guidance (2nd ed.). WHO Press. https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789289071918

citations.title: National Action Plan on Heat-Related Illnesses (NAP-HRI)
citations.authors: National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
citations.venue: Government of India, Nirman Bhawan, New Delhi
citations.implementation_role: Mandates hospital Heat Stroke Units (HSUs), emergency cooling beds, ORS corners, and daily surveillance reporting standards in India.
citations.formula_mapping: HSU Bed Need (20% of excess admissions), Emergency IV Fluids (3.5L chilled saline per patient)
citations.apa_citation: National Centre for Disease Control. (2024). National action plan on heat-related illnesses (NAP-HRI). Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India.

citations.title: Standard Clinical Operating Protocols for Emergency Heat Management
citations.authors: All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) Department of Emergency Medicine
citations.venue: AIIMS Emergency Medicine Clinical Review, New Delhi & Bhubaneswar
citations.implementation_role: Provides clinical guidance on rapid evaporative cooling, core temperature tracking, and ICD-10 syndromic distribution (sunstroke, cardiovascular, acute kidney injury, respiratory).
citations.formula_mapping: Syndromic Classification: Direct Heat (T67), Cardio (I20-I64), Renal (N17), Resp (J44)
citations.apa_citation: All India Institute of Medical Sciences. (2023). Standard clinical operating protocols for emergency management of severe heat-related illnesses. AIIMS Emergency Medicine Press.

citations.title: Ambient Temperature and Risk of Hospital Admissions: Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis
citations.authors: Phung, D., Thai, P. K., Guo, Y., Morawska, L., Rutherford, S., & Chu, C.
citations.implementation_role: Provides empirical pooled Relative Risk (RR) bounds for hospital admissions during extreme heat: all-cause admissions RR = 1.16, renal admissions RR = 1.30, and direct heatstroke RR = 2.45.
citations.formula_mapping: Emergency Surge Scaling: Bounded by Pooled Relative Risk (RR 1.16 to 1.35)
citations.apa_citation: Phung, D., Thai, P. K., Guo, Y., Morawska, L., Rutherford, S., & Chu, C. (2016). Ambient temperature and risk of cardiovascular, respiratory, and metabolic hospital admissions: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Environmental Research, 151, 804–814.

citations.title: Cause-Specific Risk of Hospital Admission Related to Extreme Heat in Older Adults
citations.authors: Bobb, J. F., Obermeyer, Z., Wang, Y., & Dominici, F.
citations.venue: JAMA: Journal of the American Medical Association, 312(24), 2659-2667
citations.implementation_role: Demonstrates compounding excess casualty admissions on consecutive heatwave days (Day 2+) due to body heat accumulation and failed nocturnal cooling.
citations.formula_mapping: Consecutive Day Multipliers: Day 1 = 1.00 | Day 2 = 1.25 | Day 3+ = 1.35
citations.apa_citation: Bobb, J. F., Obermeyer, Z., Wang, Y., & Dominici, F. (2014). Cause-specific risk of hospital admission related to extreme heat in older adults. JAMA, 312(24), 2659–2667.
